spot.html_text: Simon’s general psychology is standard Aristotelian doctrine, in many aspects derived from Albert the Great’s and Aquinas’s psychological teachings. However, as we shall see, Simon sometimes conflates their views, which suggests that he was not entirely aware of their opposition. spot.html_text: If added existence is something real, then it is actual. So, it is either a first or a second actuality. Not a first, because a first actuality is not different from the essence. Not a second, because a second actuality is an operation that presupposes actual existence. Moreover, it cannot be a third actuality, because this is contrary to Aristotelian doctrine (furthermore, it would lead to an infinite regress, as Radulphus Brito would point out). Therefore, added existence is not something real
